title: Counting baby's movements at home
what: You keep track of how often your baby moves. It is a simple way to notice whether your baby is doing well.
why: Usually in the second half of pregnancy, when movements are easy to feel. Your doctor will tell you how to count.
duration: usually up to 1 to 2 hours a day, as your doctor advises
tell_doctor: If movements have become less frequent or weaker
If the pattern of movements changed suddenly
If you are not sure how to count correctly

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Choose a time when your baby is usually active, often after a meal or in the evening.

prepare.title: Position
prepare.text: Lie on your left side or sit comfortably.

prepare.title: Notes
prepare.text: Have a notebook or an app ready to mark the movements.

bring: A notebook or phone for notes
steps: Count each movement: a push, a roll, a kick
Note the time when you reach the number you need
feel: Movements can feel different: pushes, rolls, or light fluttering
Your baby may sleep for up to 20 to 40 minutes. This is normal
after: Show your notes to the doctor at your visit
If everything is as usual, keep watching
It is important to know your baby's usual pattern
red_flags: Your baby has stopped moving or is moving much less than usual: call your doctor or the maternity hospital right away
You did not feel the movements within the time your doctor gave you: call emergency services
Bleeding or leaking fluid: call emergency services

faq.q: How many movements should there be?
faq.a: Methods differ. Most often, the goal is 10 movements within a set time. Your doctor will tell you your number.

faq.q: My baby is quiet. Can I wait until tomorrow?
faq.a: No. If there are fewer movements than usual, call your doctor or the maternity hospital right away. Do not wait.

reminders.text: Time to count your baby's movements. Lie on your side and mark each movement.
